| **Carried in its passage's telling; pointer only** | Mat 18:23 (the parable is told through 18:33–34 in 10.13) | 1 |
| **Data, with the reason** | 2Ch 36:10, Dan 11:8, 1Ki 5:17, Judg 1:35 | 4 |

| **Psa 94:20** | "Can wicked rulers be allied with you, those who frame injustice by statute?" Rule turned to injustice, set against God. Around it: "When I thought, 'My foot slips,' your steadfast love, O Lord, held me up" (94:18, uncited); "They band together against the life of the righteous" (94:21); "But the Lord has become my stronghold" (94:22) | 10.9 (the thought of falling met by steadfast love); Ch 11 *Authority as a standing* (rule that frames injustice) |

| **Isa 50:2** | "Why, when I came, was there no man; why, when I called, was there no one to answer? Is my hand shortened, that it cannot redeem?" God calls and no one answers. Two verses on, the servant: "Morning by morning he awakens; he awakens my ear to hear" (50:4, cited in 10.2) | 10.2 (not answering beside the awakened ear); 13.1 (his power questioned and asserted) |

| **1Sa 26:16** | David to Abner: "you deserve to die, because you have not kept watch over your lord, the Lord's anointed". David had refused to strike Saul (26:9–11, uncited), took the spear and jar as proof, and asks Saul: "Why does my lord pursue after his servant? For what have I done? What evil is on my hands?" (26:18). Saul: "Is this your voice, my son David?" (26:17) | 10.10 *Loyalty and honour* (a guard's duty failed; restraint toward the anointed); the hands as the seat of guilt, for signpost #1893 |

| **Dan 8:4** | The ram in the vision: "No beast could stand before him … He did as he pleased and became great". Then the goat came "in his powerful wrath" (8:6). Later, "it became great, even as great as the Prince of the host" (8:11, uncited) | 10.7 *Willing* (the will made absolute, beside Dan 11:3, 11:36); 10.15 (becoming great against the Prince); figure, read as figure |

| **1Ki 2:18, with 2:13–25** | Bathsheba meets Adonijah with "Do you come peacefully?" (2:13). He says, "You know that the kingdom was mine … However, the kingdom has turned about and become my brother's, for it was his from the Lord" (2:15). Then: "one request … do not refuse me" (2:16), Abishag. Solomon honours his mother ("rose to meet her and bowed down to her", 2:19) and promises, "I will not refuse you" (2:20). Then he reads the request as the claim: "Ask for him the kingdom also" (2:22). He swears, and Adonijah dies (2:23–25). **I read** that the verses give Solomon's reading of the request, not Adonijah's own heart | 10.10 *Fear that arrives with a person* ("Do you come peacefully?", beside 1Sa 16:4); 10.6 (a wish read as a claim); 10.10 *Loyalty and honour* (a king bows to his mother); 10.5 *The oath* (a promise not to refuse, overridden) |

| **Est 7:9** | Harbona names the gallows. Around it: "Haman stayed to beg for his life … for he saw that harm was determined against him" (7:7); the king reads Haman's fall on the couch as assault (7:8); "So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the wrath of the king abated" (7:10). All uncited | 10.10 *Plotting against another* (the plot returns on the plotter); 10.13 (anger on a misreading, and anger that abates); 10.12 (fear that sees harm determined) |

| **2Sa 12:30** (and 1Ch 20:2) | The crown placed on David's head. Joab had sent: "encamp against the city and take it, lest I take the city and it be called by my name" (12:28, uncited). Joab yields the honour of the capture to the king | 10.10 *Loyalty and honour* |

| **1Sa 25:8** | David's request to Nabal: "let my young men find favor in your eyes", grounded in "we did them no harm" (25:7). Nabal answers, "Who is David?" (25:10). David: "Every man strap on his sword!" (25:13). All uncited | 10.13 *What it rises at* (contempt for a request grounded in good done); 10.10 |

| **2Sa 19:37** | Barzillai: "let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Chimham". He gives his place to another. 19:35 and 19:38 are told in 10.7 and Ch 11 | Ch 2 *Facing death* (where one wants to die) |

| **Luk 19:12** | The nobleman's kingdom. The parable is told "because they supposed that the kingdom of God was to appear immediately" (19:11, uncited). 19:14 is told in 10.7 | 10.4 (an expectation the parable answers) |

| **2Sa 14:32** | Absalom: "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still. Now therefore let me go into the presence of the king, and if there is guilt in me, let him put me to death". Then "the king kissed Absalom" (14:33). The field-burning (14:30–31) is told in 10.10 | 10.10 *Plotting against another* (the reason behind the burning: estrangement and a demand to be seen) |
| **1Ki 2:42** | Shimei's oath. 2:43 is told in 10.5. Then: "You know in your own heart all the harm that you did to David my father" (2:44, uncited) | Ch 4 (the heart knows its own harm); 10.5 |

| **2Ch 32:11** | "Is not Hezekiah misleading you …?" with "On what are you trusting?" (32:10) and "Do you not know what I and my fathers have done?" (32:13). Trust is attacked through doubt of the leader and a record of power. The parallels (2Ki 18:20–22; Isa 36:5–7) are uncited | 10.9 (trust attacked); 10.5 (words that undermine) |

| **Est 2:2, 2:3** | After the king's anger abated, "he remembered Vashti" (2:1, told). His servants answer the remembering with a search for "beautiful young virgins … under custody", and "the young woman who pleases the king" (2:4); "This pleased the king". **I read** that the remembering is redirected by pleasure offered. The women's own will is not asked | 10.3 (what others do with a king's remembering); 10.1 *When delight is only the measure* |

| **1Ki 9:1, 9:19** (and 2Ch 8:6) | "All that Solomon desired to build" (9:1). God then appears: "I have consecrated this house … My eyes and my heart will be there for all time" (9:3, uncited). "Whatever Solomon desired to build" goes with the remnant peoples drafted as forced labour (9:19–21) | 13.1 and Ch 11 §8 (God's heart on the house); 10.6 (desire fulfilled, and at whose labour) |

| **1Ki 9:11** | Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities. "they did not please him", and "What kind of cities are these that you have given me, my brother?" (9:12–13). A gift judged and resented between allies | 10.10 *Friends, company and care* |

| **Gen 41:35** | Joseph's plan "under the authority of Pharaoh": "let Pharaoh select a discerning and wise man" (41:33); a reserve "so that the land may not perish" (41:36); "This proposal pleased Pharaoh" (41:37) | 10.7 *Planning* (foresight against a known famine) |

| **Isa 5:9** | The oath of desolation answers "Woe to those who join house to house, who add field to field, until there is no more room, and you are made to dwell alone in the midst of the land" (5:8, uncited) | 10.6 *Coveting* (adding until one is alone) |

| **Est 1:8** | "There is no compulsion … to do as each man desired". On the seventh day "the heart of the king was merry with wine" (1:10, told in 10.1 and Ch 11) | 10.1 (the feast's licence before the merry heart's command) |

| **Pro 16:15** | "In the light of a king's face there is life, and his favor is like the clouds that bring the spring rain", beside "A king's wrath is a messenger of death" (16:14, told in 10.13) | 10.10 *Holding authority over another*; Ch 2 (life from another's face) |

| **Rev 11:6** | The two witnesses' power, "as often as they desire", within "the days of their prophesying"; then they are killed (11:7) | Ch 11 *Authority as a standing* (power given for a time and used at will) |
